question.text: What year-over-year change in US Cyber Monday online spending will Adobe report for 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the year-over-year percentage change in US online spending on Cyber Monday 2026 (November 30, 2026) compared with Cyber Monday 2025, as reported by [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/) (Adobe Analytics or Adobe Digital Insights).
question.fine_print:
* If Adobe reports a dollar figure (in line with its practice in previous reports), the question will resolve as the year-over-year percentage change, calculated to four significant figures, using \$14.25 billion as the 2025 number.
* Adobe's first full-day figure will be used; later revisions will be ignored.
* Any projections published before Cyber Monday is over do not count.
* If Adobe reports only a year-over-year percentage change, the question will resolve according to Adobe's reported figure, to the highest precision used by Adobe (up to four significant figures).

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46105) which opened on 2026-11-02 18:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

I've finished searching and am writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2025-12-02: Adobe's first report put US Cyber Monday 2025 online spend at $14.25B, up 7.1% YoY. Cyber Week was $44.2B (+7.7%) and Black Friday $11.8B (+9.1%). Adobe had forecast Cyber Monday at $14.2B (+6.3%), so the actual came in slightly above. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2025/12/adobe-cyber-monday-hits-record)
- Adobe usually publishes its Cyber Monday recap the next morning, which would be about 2026-12-01. Under the fine print, if Adobe gives a dollar figure the question uses $14.25B as the base. That means:
  - $15.1B resolves as +5.965%
  - $15.0B resolves as +5.263%
  - $15.5B resolves as +8.772%

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Cyber Monday is 2026-11-30. All 2026 figures so far are projections, and projections don't count for resolution.
- Adobe's forecast says +6.2% for $15.1B, which implies a 2025 base of about $14.22B, perhaps a revised number. On the question's $14.25B base, the same $15.1B works out to about +5.97%. If Adobe's recap reports a dollar figure, the result could differ from Adobe's own headline percentage because of this base gap.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-10-08/09: Adobe reported US online spend of $9.86B during Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7), up 8.5% YoY from $9.09B. Its forecast was $9.9B (+9.2%), so the actual was essentially on forecast, slightly under. [Digital Commerce 360](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/10/08/amazon-prime-day-big-deal-days-sales-2026/)

  - Deepest electronics discounts expected on Cyber Monday, about 30%
  - The release does not mention tariffs or inflation.
- I found no November 2026 Adobe season-to-date update, and no reported actual for October 2026 as a whole.

## 4. Base rates
These are Adobe's first-reported Cyber Monday YoY figures, recalled from Adobe's past releases. I only checked 2024 and 2025 directly this session. [2024 recap](https://news.adobe.com/news/2024/12/120324-adi-cyber-monday-recap)

| Year | Cyber Monday spend | YoY |
|---|---|---|
| 2019 | $9.4B | +19.7% |
| 2020 | $10.8B | +15.1% |
| 2021 | $10.7B | -1.4% (first-ever decline) |

- Since 2022 the range has been 5.8% to 9.6%, with growth stable at about 7% over the last two years.
- How actuals compared with Adobe's own forecast (approximate, from memory):

| Year | Forecast | Actual | Beat by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | +5.1% ($11.2B) | +5.8% | ~0.7 pt |
| 2023 | +5.4% ($12.0B) | +9.6% | ~4 pts |
| 2024 | +6.1% ($13.2B) | +7.3% | ~1.2 pts |
| 2025 | +6.3% ($14.2B) | +7.1% | ~0.8 pt |

- Actuals have met or beaten the forecast four years in a row. A similar beat in 2026 would mean about +6.5% to +8% on the $14.25B base, or roughly $15.2B to $15.4B.
- Structural trend: Black Friday and Thanksgiving are growing faster than Cyber Monday as spending shifts earlier, and Adobe's 2026 forecast repeats that pattern.
- Calendar: Cyber Monday 2026 (Nov 30) falls late, the same position as in 2020 and 2015. A late Thanksgiving means a shorter season, which tends to concentrate demand into Cyber Week.
- The one 2026 data point measured so far: Prime Big Deal Days came in at +8.5%, against +7.3% for the same event in 2025.
